causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is correct (see page 6).
Turn on the hot water faucet nearest the dishwasher, let run until the water temperature stops rising.
Then start the dishwasher and turn off the faucet.
This insures the entering water is hot.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Low inlet water temperature"

symptoms.symptom: Spots and filming on glasses and flatware

causes.label: Extremely hard water
remedies: Use Jet-Dry ® or Cascade Crystal Clear® rinse agents to remove spots and prevent new film buildup.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Extremely hard water"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure water temperature is at least 120°F.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Overloading the dishwasher
remedies: Load dishwasher as shown in the Loading Place Settings section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Overloading the dishwasher"

causes.label: Improper loading
remedies: Make sure detergent is fresh.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Improper loading"

causes.label: Combination of soft water and too much detergent
remedies: This is called etching and is permanent.
To prevent this from happening, use less detergent if you have soft water.
Wash glassware in the shortest cycle that will get it clean.
Recalibrate the SmartDispense™ system if you are using it (see page 9).
Do not use the manual detergent dispenser and the SmartDispense™ at the same time.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Combination of soft water and too much detergent"

causes.label: Correct detergent wasn’t used
remedies: Use only automatic dishwasher detergents to avoid sudsing.
Cascade® and Electrasol® Automatic Dishwashing Detergents have been approved for use in all GE dishwashers.
To remove suds from the tub, open the dishwasher and let suds dissipate.
Close and latch the dishwasher.
Pump out water by touching the START/RESET pad once; then 30 seconds later, touch the START/RESET pad again.
Repeat if necessary.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Correct detergent wasn’t used"

causes.label: Rinse agent was spilled
remedies: Always wipe up rinse agent spills immediately.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Rinse agent was spilled"

causes.label: Detergent placed in manual detergent dispenser and SmartDispense™ dispenser
remedies: Use SmartDispense™ or the manual detergent dispenser, but not both.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Detergent placed in manual detergent dispenser and SmartDispense™ dispenser"

causes.label: SmartDispense™ outlet
remedies: See the Loading the dishwasher section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "SmartDispense™ outlet"

causes.label: Cap not tightened after filling the dispenser
remedies: Use a turkey baster to remove as much water as possible from the SmartDispense™ dispenser and refill it as normal.
Be sure to tighten the cap fully to prevent water from entering the dispenser.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Cap not tightened after filling the dispenser"

symptoms.symptom: Black or gray marks on dishes

causes.label: Aluminum utensils have rubbed against dishes
remedies: Remove marks with a mild, abrasive cleaner.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Aluminum utensils have rubbed against dishes"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is at least 120°F.
Select HEATED DRY.
Use HOT START, HOT WASH or ADDED HEAT options.
Select a higher cycle, such as ANTI-BACTERIA, SANI WASH or POTS & PANS.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Rinse agent dispenser is empty
remedies: Check the rinse agent dispenser and fill as required.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Rinse agent dispenser is empty"

causes.label: Some tomato-based foods can cause reddish stains
remedies: Use of the RINSE ONLY cycle after adding the dish to the load can decrease the level of staining.
GE recommends Cascade® Plastic Booster to help remove these types of stains.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Some tomato-based foods can cause reddish stains"

causes.label: Tea or coffee stains
remedies: Remove the stain by hand, using a solution of 1/2 cup bleach and 3 cups warm water.
WARNING Before cleaning interior, wait at least 20 minutes after a cycle for the heating elements to cool down.
Failure to do so can result in burns.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Tea or coffee stains"

causes.label: Fuse is blown or circuit breaker is tripped
remedies: Replace fuse or reset circuit breaker.
Remove any other appliances from the circuit.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Fuse is blown or circuit breaker is tripped"

causes.label: Power is turned off
remedies: In some installations, the power to the dishwasher is provided through a wall switch, often located next to the disposer switch.
Make sure it is on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Power is turned off"

causes.label: Control panel is locked
remedies: Unlock control panel.
See page 5 or 7.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Control panel is locked"

causes.label: Reboot your control
remedies: Turn off power to the dishwasher (circuit breaker or wall switch) for 30 seconds; then turn back on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Reboot your control"

symptoms.symptom: Control panel lights go off when you’re setting controls

causes.label: Time too long between touching of selected pads
remedies: Each pad must be touched within 30 seconds of the others.
To relight, touch any pad again, or unlock and relatch door.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "Time too long between touching of selected pads"

causes.label: This is normal
remedies: Warm, moist air comes through the vent by the door latch during drying and when water is being pumped out.
This is necessary for drying.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "This is normal"

symptoms.symptom: Sanitized light does not illuminate at the end of the cycle

causes.label: The door was opened and the cycle was interrupted during or after the main wash portion
remedies: Do not interrupt the cycle anytime during or after main wash.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 14: "The door was opened and the cycle was interrupted during or after the main wash portion"
